claims.text: The local catalog places Expansion Sheet Series 3 Green on November 24, 1998.
The local release models 53 unique catalog rows and carries the count caveat that the release is often described as 36 standard cards plus 17 special/non-standard cards.
The local release identifies the product as glossy Vending/Expansion Sheet cards, with Pokellector as source and Bulbapedia caption metadata used for artist-credit texture.

The pre-English symbol-status matrix marks Expansion Sheet Series 3 Green as prints_without_rarity_symbol: no, high confidence, with trap consequence that vending cards are glossy and not the Base No Rarity lane.

The release has a common-rarity surface but contains high-memory rows including Mewtwo, Scyther, Kangaskhan, Ooyama's Pikachu, Imakuni? cards, rule-format cards, and adventure/location cards; common rarity is not a proxy for low collector meaning.

The local sheet carries a wide illustrator/personality roster including Nobuyuki Habu, Atsuko Nishida, Tomokazu Komiya, Masako Yamashita, Ooyama/OOYAMA, Imakuni?, Hironobu Yoshida, Kazuhiko Nishihara, Keiji Kinebuchi, and others; several special rows have no surfaced illustrator credit.

Series 3 Green matters because the vending-sheet form stretches from ordinary Kanto rows into rule experiments, non-playable personality cards, Imakuni? weirdness, Ooyama visual humor, and location/adventure prompts. It is a sheet that starts as catalog and ends as culture.

Agents should preserve Japanese title, date, row number, glossy vending-sheet format, Common rarity signal, the 36-plus-17 count caveat, special/non-standard card status, artist/personality credit source, and no/not-Base-No-Rarity symbol boundary before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Expansion Sheet Series 3 Green — where vending turns into a funhouse
narrative.why_it_matters: Series 3 Green is the vending sheet that starts like a set and then slips sideways. Yes, there are familiar Kanto creatures and Mewtwo gravity, but the back half becomes rules, puzzles, personality cards, Ooyama, Imakuni?, and little scenes that feel closer to Pokémon culture than to ordinary booster structure. That is why the count caveat matters: 36 standard cards plus a strange special tail is not just bookkeeping, it is the shape of the object. For agents, Green is a warning and a joy: never identify by character name alone when the route itself is this expressive.
